title: Equals() implementation may throw NullPointerException when given null.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Prefer instanceof to getClass when implementing Object#equals. Note that this may be a behaviour change.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Classes that override equals should also override hashCode.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: An equality test between objects with incompatible types always returns false.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Method overrides Object.equals but does not have @Nullable on its parameter.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: == NaN always returns false; use the isNaN methods instead.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: The contract of Object.equals() states that for any non-null reference value x, x.equals(null) should return false. If x is null, a NullPointerException is thrown. Consider replacing equals() with the == operator.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: == must be used in equals method to check equality to itself or an infinite loop will occur.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: The contract of #equals states that it should return false for incompatible types, while this implementation may throw ClassCastException.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Implementing #equals by just comparing hashCodes is fragile. Hashes collide frequently, and this will lead to false positives in #equals.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Comparing different pairs of fields/getters in an equals implementation is probably a mistake.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.
